title: Admin onboarding & access request prioritization gate (RBAC/SSO/SCIM)
creator: Aisha N'Diaye
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are submitting admin & access requests (RBAC role creation, SSO/SAML integrations, SCIM provisioning, org policy exceptions) through multiple channels (billing, support, account execs). Current handling is ad hoc: delayed routing, inconsistent prioritization, and unclear SLAs. This causes customer friction for launch-critical integrations and increases handoffs for Solutions/Support/Eng.

Goals: 1) Define a single lightweight intake + scoring gate for non-bug admin requests that surfaces priority, compliance risk, and engineering cost. 2) Produce deterministic routing rules and SLA targets for triage, investigation, and schedule decisions (self-serve, config work, eng backlog). 3) Create playbooks and templates for Solutions and Support to accelerate resolution and reduce unnecessary engineering churn.

Scope: Non-bug, non-incident requests related to admin/access: RBAC role model changes, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning changes, organization-level policy exceptions, delegated admin requests, and data residency access approvals. Out of scope: security incidents, P0 outages, and large migrations (>50k users) which follow the enterprise security intake flow.

Proposed solution summary: 1) Intake form (internal) with structured fields: customer size, user counts, legal/compliance flags, desired SLA, sensitive scopes requested, estimated engineering effort (small/medium/large), required rollout date, and point of contact. 2) Scoring rubric to compute a triage score combining customer tier, launch-critical flag, compliance risk, and estimated effort. 3) Routing policies mapping score bands to outcomes: auto-accept (self-serve guide + docs), scheduled in Solutions/Support work queue, product review required (PM + Security), or Engineering backlog with committed SLA. 4) Templates & checklists to standardize handoffs (SSO checklist, SCIM provisioning validation steps, RBAC modeling primer). 5) Dashboard for visibility: per-month intake volume, median time-to-triage, percent auto-resolved, and engineering-hours avoided.

Success metrics: - Reduce mean time-to-first-response for admin requests from ~5 business days to <24 hours. - Increase auto-resolve/self-serve rate for low-risk requests to >=40% within 8 weeks. - Decrease number of engineering clarifying messages by 60% (measure from ticket threads). - SLA attainment: 90% of triaged requests assigned to the correct queue within 24 hours.

Acceptance criteria: - Intake form deployed in internal Tools (Forms/Linear integration) and used for all new admin requests. - Scoring algorithm documented and validated with sample historical requests. - Routing policies implemented as runbook for Solutions/Support and an automation prototype (Zapier/Workato or internal integration) to label tickets. - Dashboard MVP (Looker/Grafana) showing intake volume and time-to-triage. - Playbooks and templated responses live in Confluence and accessible to support/solutions.

Risks & trade-offs: - Over-automation may misclassify complex requests; mitigation: manual review fallback and safety net with audit logs. - Additional latency for high-touch onboarding if score thresholds are miscalibrated; mitigation: pilot with a small set of accounts and weekly calibration. - Security review may add time for compliance-sensitive requests; we will bake a fast-path for previously vetted partners.
